ca_pete.blurb: Pete is a boulder cluster on Bishop Peak above the city of San Luis Obispo, on the Central Coast. Walking up the main trail, it is the group on your left, with the neighbouring Chlorissa boulder on the right. It holds nine problems, spanning V0 up to V8, with most of the weight in the V5 to V6 range. The lines lean steeper and more overhanging than the slabbier boulder next door, with higher top-outs and less forgiving falls, so a pair of crash pads and a spotter make sense.

ca_goodrich_boulder.blurb: Goodrich Boulder is a single block in the western part of Camp 4 in Yosemite Valley, next to the old paved trail that threads through the boulders above the campground, directly across from Wine Boulder. It carries nine problems from V0 up to V7, with the bulk in the easy-to-moderate range and a pair of harder lines at the top end. Tendons Give and Moss Monkey are the lines most climbers come for. The block is quick to reach on foot from camp, and it makes a handy addition to a session on the neighbouring Camp 4 boulders.

ca_central_joyless_area.blurb: Central Joyless Area is a small wall on the rim of a canyon within the Sad Boulders, in the Volcanic Tableland outside Bishop. The wall faces east and sits roughly fifty feet up the canyon from the Molly Area. Nine problems run from V0 to V4, with four of them at the easiest grade, and the lines are all on vertical rock above flat landings. The grades suit newer boulderers and warm-ups.

ca_lightning_bolt_crag_2.blurb: Lightning Bolt Crag is a small crag in the BMX Crags section of the Horsemen's Center, in Apple Valley in the Mojave high desert. It sits just south of the parking area, with the Black Corridor close by to the east. Nine routes mix cracks and faces across sport, trad and top-rope lines, nearly all between 5.8 and 5.10. Crack Dream, Thunder Buddy, Ride the Lightning and Bolts of Fury stand out among them. The crag suits climbers working through the lower and middle grades who want a short walk and a quick lap-based session.

ca_mystical_tricks_cliff.blurb: Mystical Tricks Cliff is a sport wall on the western side of the Central Gorge in the Owens River Gorge, near Bishop in the Eastern Sierra, sitting before the Roadside Boulders. Nine bolted routes cover 5.8 to 5.11, with most in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers moving up from the 5.9 level as well as those on harder lines. The surrounding Central Gorge is a dense, busy sport area, with the Pub Wall and Warm Up Wall among its neighbours.

ca_liam_boulder.blurb: Liam Boulder is one of three boulders in the Upper Oasis cluster at Yuba Gap, along the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe, at roughly 5,700 feet. It is the smallest of the three and stands about ten feet from the next boulder over. One side is a very low-angle slab, while the other has more featured faces. Nine problems range from VB to V3, so it is well suited to beginners, to warm-ups and to climbers who like gentle grades.

ca_frank_s_boulder.blurb: Frank's Boulder sits in the Trailside Area of the Tramway zone in the San Jacinto Mountains above Palm Springs, at about 8,500 feet. Nine problems cover V2 to V7, with long rails and incut holds, and the landings are mostly good. The Terminator, Frank's Roof and Frank's Problem are the most-repeated lines, while a handful of variations and sloper traverses sit at the top of the range. The elevation keeps the air cooler than on the desert floor below.
